To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ECDSs become more sensitive to environmental conditions, as the excitation frequency is increased; 2) the sensitivity of the ECDSs to the humidity of the air is a function of the excitation frequency and the SRF of the sensing coil; and 3) the minimum SRF of the coil can be calculated, given the allowable displacement error and the expected change in relative humidity.
“The SRF of the ECDS coil should be increased to mitigate the effect of the parasitic capacitance, in order to maintain the sensor performance in a humid environment.”

the SRF requirement of the ECDS sensing coil is proportional to the square root of the humidity variation and inversely proportional to the allowable displacement error, and that the SRF of the coil can be increased by increasing the number of coil layers, by reducing the coil thickness, or by using a material with a higher electrical conductivity.
